S.C. Das, Advocate, with Mokbul Ahmed, Advocate ------ for the appellant. 
A.K.M Shafiqur Rahman, Advocate with Mostafa Niaz Mahammad and Momtazuddin Ahmed, Advocates ------- for the respondents.

Vs.

full_judgment:
2. The case for the plaintiff respondent Haji Abdul Malek Sowdager is that defendant No.1 is a Wald Estate known as Haji Abdul Latif Sheristadar Wakf Estate. The said Wakf Estate was brought into existence by one Abdul Latif, retired Sheristadar by Wakfnama Ext. G dated 11-2-1919. The Wakf property consisted of 14.30 acres of urban as well as rural properties. During his life time the Wakif Abdul Latif was to be the Mutwalli. After his death his son Mia Mohammad Eahya became the next Mutwalli for first live years in term of the Wakf deed Ext. G. Mia Mohammad Eahya on behalf of the defendant appellant Wakf Estate made an application to defendant No.5 Chittagong Development Authority and on that application defendant No.5 C.D.A. allotted 276 acres (equivalent to 14.86 kathas—about 12 gandas) of land appertaining to commercial plot No.5 at C.D.A. Jubilee Road, Chittagong for giving lease of the same for a period of 99 years on the terms contained in the said letter of allotment. The premium for the said land was fixed at Taka 5,00,000/- per acre (i.e. Taka 10,000/- per ganda). The first installment of Taka 40,000/- was to be paid within 10 days from the date of the said allotment letter. The Defendant No.1 Wakf Estate was short of fund and was not in a position to pay the premium of the land to defendant No.5 C.D.A. The then Mutwalli Mia Mohammad Eahya made an application to proforma defendant No.4 Administrator of Wakf to transfer about 9 gandas of land out of the said alloted Land with a view to raise necessary fund to pay the premium to pro-defendant No.5 C.D.A. The Administrator of Wakfs (pro-defendant No.4) by memo No.1681 dated 30-3-66 Ext. X granted permission to the following effect: - 

 With reference to his petition dated 28-3-66 on the above subject he is informed that he is permitted to transfer 9 (nine) gandas of land as prayed for out of 14 gandas allotted to the Wakf Estate by the C.D.A. 

 Mia Mohammad Eahya on behalf of the Wakf Estate, Chittagong took an advance from pro-defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum (wife of pro-defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan) by verbally entering into a contract for sale of 9.90 kattas of land to Mrs. Hamidi Begum pro-defendant No.6. Mia Mohammad Eahya, the then Mutwalli paid the first premium of Taka 70,000/- to pro-defendant No.5 C.D.A. who thereafter executed the registered lease deed Ext,5 dated 24-1-67 in favour of defendant No.1 Wakf Estate for the said 14.86 kattas of land of commercial plot No.5, C.D.A. Jubilee Road. The agreement Ext.1 between the Wakf Estate and defendant No.6. Mrs, Hamidi Begum for sale of 9.90 kattas (equivalent to 8 agandas 1 kara) in the northern portion of the said commercial plot No.5 C.D.A. Jubilee Road., Commercial Area in favour of defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum and an lrrevccable General Power of Attorney Ext.2 between the Wakf Estate (defendant No.1) represented by. Mutwalli Haji Mia Mohammad Eahya and defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan (husband of defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum) was executed on the same date 26-1-67 authorising him (defendant No.7) to construct a building on the same land at a cost of Taka 2,00,000/- and to execute a sale deed in favour of defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum after completion of the construction. For various reasons the said proposed building was not constructed and the sale deed was not executed and registered in favour of Mrs. Hamidi Begum. In the meantime defendant No.2 S.W. Siddique, son of Haji Mia Mohammad Eahya became the Mutwalli. It was settled between defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique, the previous Mutwalli and defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum that if the Wakf Estate defendant No.1 can arrange to refund the consideration amount of Taka 81,730/- to defendant No.6 Mrs Hamidi Begum, she shall release the Wakf Estate from the contract of said Ext.1 along with the Power of Attorney Ext.2. Defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique as the Mutwalli of defendant No I then proposed to sell the said 8 gandas 1 kara of the suit land and the plaintiff Haji Abdul Malek Sowdagar agreed to purchase the same. After negotiation the terms and conditions of sale and the price of the land were fixed and an advance of Taka 1,15,000/- was paid by the plaintiff to defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique representing defendant No. 1 Wakf Estate as per memorandum of agreement Ext.6 dated 4-9-74. It was agreed that the defendant No.1 Wakf Estate would sell to the plaintiff the said land @ Taka 25,000/- per ganda, that a power of attorney would be executed as usual, that Income-Tax clearance certificate would be obtained by defendant No.1, that the plaintiff would refund to defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum earnest money that was taken by defendant No.1 from defendant No.6 and that the plaintiff would take back the bainama Ext. l from the defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum. The Memorandum of agreement Ext.6 was written by the plaintiff in defendant No.2's letter-head sheet of his personal firm "Cine Services" in own hand and the Mutwalli defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique put his signature on the same with date 4-9-74. P.W.2 Sayedul Huq also signed the same on 4-9-74 as an attesting witness. On the same date 4-9-74 defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique handed over the original lease deed Ext.5 dated 24-1-67 granted by C.D.A. (defendant No.5) and other papers to the plaintiff. Defendant No.2 as Mutwalli of defendant No.1 for completion of the said sale transaction signed on that very date two applications for Income-Tax Clearance Certificate along with two duplicates Ext.10 series and handed them over to the plaintiff. Two separate schedules showing equal half of the suit land i.e. 4.80 kattas each Ext.10A series were also signed on that date by defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique. Defendant No.2 then sent P.W.3 Hemayetulla with the plaintiff to defendant No.7 and the plaintiff thereafter refunded Taka 81,730/- to defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begun on behalf of defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique in presence P.W.3 Md. Hemayetulla, an employee of defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan. P.W.4 and defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum on 5-12-74 executed the deed of cancellation of the agreement Ext.3. Defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan on 5-12-74 executed the Memorandum Ext.4 cancelling Irrevocable General Power of Attorney. Defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique, the Mutwalli again received a sum of Taka 3,000/- as per cheque No.313118 (counter foil Ext.8 dated 18-12-78) of the Eastern Marcantile Bank. The said cheque the counter foil of which has been marked Ext.8 was received by defendant No.2's employee Sree Kali Prasad Dey as per receipt Ext.9 by signing the same on 18-12-74 in respect of payment towards earnest money for the purchase of the same land. The pass Book Ext.19 of the plaintiff in respect of his account No.1114 of Eastern Marcantile Bank Ltd., Sadarghat, Chittagong has been exhibited to show that Taka 3000/- was in cash on 18-12-74. Thus in three instalments of Taka 1,15,000/-, Taka 81,730/- and Taka 3000/-the plaintiff in all paid Taka 1,99,730/- to defendant No.1 the Wakf Estate as part payment of consideration money out of a total consideration money of Taka 2,06,250/- at the rate of Taka 25,000/- per ganda for purchase of the suit land measuring 8 gandas 1 kara. In the meantime defendant No.5 C.D.A. passed the resolution dated 12-11-74 (Ext.18) to the following effect:-- 

 4. Defendant No.2 on behalf of defendant No.1 filed written a statement on 17-9-76 stating that the suit is barred under section 23 of the Contract Act in view of the provision of clause 19 of the lease deed Ext.5 wherein it has been provided that the tenant shall not sell, charge, mortgage, exchange, gift away or otherwise assign, sublet, encumber or in any way part with or dispose of the demised property or any part thereof before the construction, and appurtenance covenanted to he erected and such transfer without construction shall be void. In view of the provision of section 29 of the Contract Act an agreement, the meaning of which is not certain, or is not capable of being made certain, is void. It is true that the defendant No.1 Wakf Estate through previous Mutwalli took lease of 14.86 kattas of lands in plot No.5 C.D.A. Jubilee Road, Commercial Area by lease deed dated 24-1-67 from defendant No.5 C.D.A. An agreement for sale dated 26-1-67 was also executed between defendant No.1 Wakf Estate and defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum. On receipt of Taka 81,730/- an Irrevocable Power of Attorney was also executed in favour of defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan. The defendant No.5 allotted the said plot at a premium of Taka 10,000/- per ganda. The then Mutwalli of the Wakf Estate arranged with defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan and his wife defendant No.6 Hamidi Begum to share in buying the plot as the Wakf Esate defendant No.1 did not have sufficient fund to buy the whole plot. It was decided that the whole plot would be bought in the name of the Wakf Estate and proportionate lands would he transferred later on to Mrs. Hamidi Begum defendant No.6 and for such purpose, necessary permission was obtained by the then Mutwalli from the Administrator of Wakfs, Dhaka (defendant No.4). As C.D.A. rules would not permit sale of portion of a plot to a third person unless constructions had been made, the then Mutwalli entered into an agreement with Mrs. Hamidi Begum and granted Irrevocable Power of Attorney of her husband defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan to transfer 8 gandas 1 kara of the suit plot with a building to be constructed by him. The then Mutwalli of the Wakf Estate died. Defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum and her husband defendant No.7 expressed their willingness to rescind the agreement due to the changed political situation in the country on repayment of Taka 81,730/- paid by defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum to the previous Mutwalli. Defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique agreed to the proposal and was on the look out for a possible buyer to raise fund for the purpose as well as for the purpose of construction in the remaining part of the lands. Defendant No.2 on behalf of defendant No.1 did not enter into any written contract such as Memorandum of agreement Ext.6 with the plaintiff. The plaintiff was known to the defendant No.2 from before. In the early part of 1974, the plaintiff proposed to purchase the 8 gandas 1 kara of land at the rate of Taka 40,000/- per gonda and also proposed to pay 50% of the total consideration money to defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique. It was agreed that the documents from defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum would be released on payment and necessary permission will be obtained from prescribed authorities by defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique and thereafter the agreement for sale would be made. These proposal were accepted by the defendant in the early part of 1974 on the express oral agreement making the time for completion of the transfer to be made by 31-12-74 and the time was the essence of the contract. During the time of negotiation defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique expressed his intention to purchase a scooter and asked the plaintiff to sell one to the defendant. In that connection the plaintiff stated that in order to sell a scooter, permission from the Deputy Commissioner is necessary. The plaintiff gave assurance to the defendant to obtain such permission and asked the defendant to give to the plaintiff some letter-head slips of the defendant duly signed by him for making necessary application to the Deputy Commissioner and other authorities as may be necessary in this connection. The defendant No.2 in good faith gave his signature in blank letter head sheet of his personal business firm "Cine Services" at 113A, Jubilee Road, Chittagong with his signature thereon, The plaintiff has fraudulently utilised the signed blank letter-head sheet for the purpose of fabricating the alleged agreement in order to make wrongful gain by causing wrongful loss to the defendants. Defendant No.2 did not enter into any such contract for sale nor did defendant No.2 grant any receipt for Taka 1,15,000/- as alleged by the plaintiffs. The alleged signed agreement (Ext.6) is fabricated and fraudulent. No contract for sale was made by the defendant No.2 on behalf of defend-ant No.1 with plaintiff on 4-9-74 on the basis of a consideration at the rate of Taka 25,000/- per ganda. No term and condition as alleged was written down on any paper on 4-9-74 and no acknowledgement receipt of Taka 1,15,000/-was made by the Defendant No.2 on 4-9-74 Gr on any other date. No papers were written or signed or filed on 4-9-74 for Income Tax Clearance nor any such paper was handed over to the plaintiff. The verbal negotiations and agreement for sale took place long before on 4-9-74 between plaintiff and defendant No.2. The plaintiff promised to complete 'the transaction within 31-12-74 at the rate of Taka 40,000/-per ganda and also undertook to pay 50% of the total consideration money as earnest money. It was agreed that after the payment of the present money by the plaintiff bainanama would he executed containing the terms and conditions for sale. The defendant No.2 signed blank Income Tax Clearance application well after 4-9-74 and not on 4-9-74 as alleged. The plaintiff failed to pay the 50% of the consideration money as .earnest money and at the expiry of 31-12-74 the said oral contract with the plaintiff fell through due to failure of the plaintiff to comply with the terms of the oral contract. So there is no subsisting contract. It farther appears that taking advantage of the circumstances the plaintiff without making payment to the Mutwalli Defendant No.2 as agreed upon has made fraudulent deals with Mrs. Hamidi Begum defendant No.6. The plaintiff came to the defendant No.2's business premises on 4-9-74 and paid Taka 15,000/- and requested the defendant to wait for sometime. The plaintiff was given receipt. For the said amount on the letter-head of the Wakf Estate, thereafter on 19-11-74 the plaintiff paid a further stun of Taka 10,000/-. Thus the plaintiff paid only a total sum of Taka 25,000/- in all in part payment of the agreed consideration money at the rate of Taka 40,000/- per ganda. No other payment was made by the plaintiff to defendant No.2. On the date of payment of Taka 10,000/- the plaintiff was given fresh receipt for total payment of Taka 25,000/- in the letter-head form of the Wakf Estate and defendant No.2 kept copy of the said text with himself. The plaintiff has collusively obtained documents from the defendant Nos.6 and 7. The alleged payment made by the plaintiff to defendant Nos.6 and 7 cannot bind the defendant Nos.1 and 2. The specific performance of contract is an equitable relief to which the plaintiff is not entitled. The Wakf Estate will suffer great injury if specific performance as prayed for is granted. 

 5. The present Mutwalli S.M. Anwar (brother of defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique) on behalf of the Wakf Estate fired additional written statement on 30-12-78 stating that the previous Mutwalli defendant No.2 committed acts against the interest of the Wald Estate. Defendant No.2 was removed by the Wakf Administrator from the office of Mutwalli and in his place S.M. Anwar the present Mutwalli was appointed by the defendant. No.4. As per Wakfnama the Mutwalli has got no right to transfer. The alleged permission given by the Administrator of Wakf defendant No.4 to the previous Mutwalli Haji Mohammad Yahya has lost its force with the death of Haji Md. Yahya. The permission was accorded to sell the property to a particular individual. As that contract has failed, the permission has lost its Force. The plaintiff is not entitled to get any benefit out of such permission. The permission was not accorded to defendant No.2 who therefore had no authority to enter into an agreement for sale on behalf of Defend-ant No.1 with the plaintiff. After Haji Md. Yahya Mr. A.N.M. Wahed became Mutwalli who also did not act on the alleged permission. The land is vacant. In terms of the lease between the Wakf Estate Defendant No.1 and the C.P.A. Defendant No.5 any agreement to transfer before any construction is prohibited and void. As such the agreement is an unenforceable. 

 6. 4 witnesses were examined on behalf of the plaintiff. S.M. Anwar, the present Mutwalli was examined as the sole witness for the Wakf Estate defendant No.1. 

 7. The learned Subordinate Judge on a discussion of evidence found that the plaintiff on behalf of the Wakf Estate Defendant No.1 paid Taka 81,730/- to defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum, that Ext.6 (the memorandum of agreement) is a genuine document executed by defendant No.2 on behalf of defendant No.1, that the plaintiff paid Taka 1,15,000/- to defendant No.1 through its Mutwalli defendant No.2 on 4-9-74 in pursuance the contract of sale of the suit land, that the plaintiff paid Taka 3000/-in favour of defendant No.1 by issuing cheque (counter foil Ext.8) which was encashed on 18-12-74, that the application for Income Tax Clearance Certificates Ext.10 series are genuine and bear the signatures of defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique admittedly, that defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique was not removed from office of Mutwalli for any misconduct in con-section his deal with the plaintiff or for any other misconduct, that there is nothing to show that the ex-Mutwalli defendant No.2 acted in collusion with plaintiff and that defendant No. 1 through its Mutwalli defendant No.2 contracted to sell the suit land to the plaintiff for Taka 2,06,250/- at the rate of Taka 25,000/- per ganda and received Taka 1,99,730/- towards consideration money leaving a balance of Taka 6,520/- on payment of which the plaintiff is entitled to enforce the contract. On these findings the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff as aforesaid. Thereafter this appeal has been preferred by Defendant No.1. 

 9. The plaintiff P.W.1 Haji Abdul Malek Sowdagar deposed that the Haji Abdul Latif Sowdagar Wakf Estate (Defendant No.1) took lease of 276 acre (14.86 kathas) including the suit land from Defendant No.5 Chittagong Development Authority under the original lease agreement Ext.5 dated 24-1-67 which was handed over to the plaintiff by the previous Mutawalli Defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique, brother of the present Mutawalli S.M. Anwar. Defendant Not also gave him Ext. X, the order of the Wakf Administrator giving permission to sell 9 gandas out of 14 gandas of suit plot. Permission of the Administrator of Wakfs Ext. X is dated 30-3-66 granted in favour of the previous Mutawalli Md. Yahia, father of S.M. Siddique and S.M. Anwar. P.W.1 also produced the undisputed lease agreement Ext.1 dated 26-1-67 executed by the previous Mutawalli Haji Md. Yahia in favour of defendant No.6 Hamidi Begurn in respect of 8 gandas 1 kara comprising the specific separated northern portion of C.D.A. plot No.5, Jubilee Road, Chittagong. He also produced the undisputed power of attorney Ext.2 dated 26-1-67 executed by Haji Md. Yahya in favour of defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan, husband of Defendant No.6. It appears from memo of agreement Ext.1 that Defendant No.6 paid Taka 81,730/- to Haji Md. Yahia, Mutawalli of the Wakf Estate Defendant No.1 as price of land and proposed to construct a building thereon at a cost of Taka 2,00,000/- in accordance with the duly approved plan of the C.D.A. But due to various supervening factors Defendant No.6 and Defend-ant No.7 did rot like to proceed with the contract and wanted to rescind the contract and get a refund of their money. Defendant No.7 M.A. Hasan has been examined as a witness in this case. In the meantime previous Mutawalli Haji Md. Yahia had died. Defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique as Mutawalli of the Wakf Estate proposed to sell the suit land to the plaintiff and informed him that if the money paid by defendant No.6 Hamidi Begum was paid back to her, Defendant No.6 (and her husband) would forego their claim. The plaintiff agreed to purchase the suit land. Defendant No.2 as Mutawalli agreed to sell the suit land to the plaintiff at the rate of Taka 25,000/- per ganda. The total price of the suit land was agreed by the defendant No.2 and the plaintiff to be Taka 2,06,250/-. On 4-9-74 P.W.1 paid Taka 1,15,000/- on the terms and conditions written in the letter-head sheet Ext.6 of Defendant No.2's firm "Cine Services". At the dictation of defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique plaintiff P.W.1 Haji Abdul Malek wrote the contents of the agreement Ext.6. Defendant No.2 put his signature beneath the contents of agreement Ext.6. The plaintiff put his signature also. P.W.2 Md. Sayedul Huq also put his signature as an attesting witness. P.W.2 Md. Sayedul Huq has deposed that in his presence P.W.I plaintiff paid Defendant Not S.M. Siddique Taka 1,15,000/- on 4-9-74 as earnest money for purchase of the suit land in the office or Defendant No.2, that defendant No.2 acknowledged the same by assigning below the contents of the letter-head sheet Ext.6 of his "Cine Services" that the price was settled between them at the rate of Taka 25,000/- per ganda and that defendant No.2 handed over the lease deed Ext.5, the map (construction plan Ext.7), permission Ext. X and other papers. Defendant No.2 did not come to the witness box to deny the genuineness of the agreement Ext.6 which was signed by him on 4.9.74. Defendant No.2 had given a story in his written statement that he had put his signature in his blank letter-head slip and gave the same to the plaintiff for obtaining permission of the Deputy Commissioner for the purchase of a scooter. Defendant No.2 thus had to admit that he put his signature in the letter head slip of his firm but wanted to explain it away by introducing a false story which story he did not come forward to state by becoming a witness at the trial. From the evidence of P.W.1 plaintiff and P.W.1's brother-in-law P.W.2 Md. Sayedul Huq the genuineness of the agreement Ext.6 is proved and the payment of Taka 1,15,000/-by the plaintiff to defendant No.2 out of the total price of Taka 2,06,250/- at the rate of Taka 25,000/- per ganda is also proved the plaintiff deposed that defendant No.2 handed over to him Exts. 1-5 Ext. X, building construction plan Ext.7, copy of C.D.A.'s certificate of handing over of possession of the suit plot (Ext.X-2), the allotment letter and Mutawalli Md. Yahia's affidavit Ext.X-3. Production of these documents in court from the custody of the plaintiff establishes the truth of the statement of P.W.1, the plaintiff. P.W.1, the plaintiff also produced before the court duly filled in applications to the Income Tax Officer Ext.10, 10(a), 10(b) and 10(c) and all of them have been duly signed by defendant No.2. Thus genuineness of the aforesaid agreement of sale Ext.6 between the parties as stated by P.W.1 is established beyond doubt. 

 10. P.W.1 the plaintiff states that according to the direction of defendant No.2 he paid Taka 81,730/- at Dhaka to defendant No.6 Hamidi Begum (through her husband defendant No.7) as further part payment of consideration money for the suit land. While deposing on commission at Dhaka in presence of the appellant Mutawalli D,W.1 S.M. Anwar witness M.A. Hassan staled, that P.W.1 the plaintiff paid Taka 81,730/- to his wife defendant No.6 through him in presence of his employee P.W.3 Hamayetullah who also stated in his evidence that defendant No.2 entered into contract to sell the suit land to plaintiff on the basis of prior agreement with defendant Nos.6 and 7, that defendant No.2 sent him to defendant No.6 at Dhaka along with the plaintiff and that after the plaintiff refunded the entire consideration money (Taka 81,730/-) of the earlier agreement to defendant No.6 and her husband, the latter returned the original agreement, power of attorney and that defendant No.6 also executed the deed of cancellation of agreement Ext.3 dated 3-12-74 in which the plaintiff, defendant No.7, ones Zahiruddin and P.W.3 Hemayetulla signed as attesting witnesses. P.W.3 Hemayetulla also stated that he filled in the Income Tax Forms Exts. 10, 10(a), 10(b) and 10(c), that the plaintiff wrote the attached schedules, that defendant No.2 made corrections in the schedules under his initials and defendant No.2 signed each of the said Income Tax applications in his presence. Thus from the evidence of P.W.1 the plaintiff, P.W.3 Hemayetulla and witness M.A. Hassan (Defendant No.7) it has been proved beyond doubt that the plaintiff paid Taka 81,730/- to defendant No.6 on behalf of defendant No.2 in pursuance of the agreement of sale of the suit land with defendant No.2 (Mutawalli of defendant No. 1 the Wakf Estate) for rescinding the agreement entered into by the previous Mutawalli Md. Yahia with Mrs. Hamidi Begum defendant No.6. This amount of Taka 81,730/-was paid by the plaintiff as further part payment of consideration money fixed for the purchase of the suit land. 

 11. P.W.1 the plaintiff also deposed that he paid a further sum of Taka 3000/- by Eastern Marcantile Bank, Sadarghat Branch, Chittagong cheque bearing E.C. 18/8 No. 313118 dated 18-12-74 of his Savings Account No.1114 in favour of the then Mutawalli S.M. Siddique (defendant No.2). The counterfoil of this cheque is Ext.8. P.W.1 the plaintiff handed over this cheque to defendant No.2's employee Kaliprasad Dey who received the same granting the receipt Ext.9 dated 18-12-74 stating that he received the same according to the instruction of defendant No.2 as part payment towards the price of the suit land. The Pass Book Ext.11 also shows that Taka 3000/- was encashed on 18-12-74. Therefore the plaintiff has also proved that he paid a further sum of Taka 3000/- on 18-12-74 to the then Mutawalli defendant No.2 as part payment of the consideration money for the suit land is pursuance of the earlier agreement Ext.6 dated 4-9-74. Defendant No.5 the Chittagong Development Authority by their Resolution dated 12-11-74 (Ext. 18) allowed transfer of unconstructed plots if the allotment was not less than five years old and if the allottee had made full payment of all the dues provided a transfer fee of Taka 500/- only per katha or part is paid to the Chittagong Development Authority defendant No.5. The plaintiff P.W.1 was always ready to pay the balance amount to defendant No.2, the then Mutawalli but no kabala was executed by defendant No.2 on behalf of defendant No.1 the Wakf Estate. The plaintiff P.W.1 through his Advocate Mr. A. Mannan sent the formal letter Ext.12 dated 22-1-76 to defendant No.2 (Mutawalli) to receive the balance consideration money, to obtain the permission of the C.D.A. (defendant No.5) and to execute the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff. Defendant No.2 through his Advocate first gave the reply Ext.13 dated 24-2-76 intimating him that a reply would be sent by hint within a week. Defendant No.2 thereafter through his Advocate gave his reply Ext. 13(a) (wrongly dated 6-1-76) denying the contract as stated by the plaintiff and making out a false story of contract of sale of suit land at the rate of Taka 40,000/- per ganda and introducing a false story of advance of Taka 21,000/- only in all by two instalments. The plaintiff then instituted the present suit on 24-3-76 for specific performance of the contract. 

 12. In his evidence the present Mutawalli D.W.1 S.M. Anwar, (brother of defendant No.2 the previous Mutawalli) who became Mutawalli from 25-3-78 stated that his brother previous Mutawalli defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique did not enter into any agreement of sale and did not receive any money from the plaintiff for the suit land, that the agreement Ext.6 is a collusive creation, that the deeds of cancellation Ext.4 and Ext.3 are collusive creations that defendant No.2 got the suit filed by the plaintiff in order of grab the suit property, that defend-ant No.2 has been removed from Mutawalliship for such misconduct, that the Wakf Estate paid the money to Hamidi Begum (defendant No.6), that the suit land now sells at the rate of about Taka 70 or 80 thousand per katha and that the plaintiff is not entitled to got a kabala from the Wakf Estate defendant No.1. In view of the unimpeachable oral and documentary evidences produced by the plaintiff discussed above the aforesaid statement of D.W.1 S.M. Anwar, brother of defendant No.2 is palpably untrue. There is absolutely no reliable material whatsoever to show that defendant No.2 was removed from Mutawalliship for any misconduct. D.W.1 S.M. Anwar admits that he attended commission for taking the deposition of defendant No.7 M.A. Hassan, husband of D.W. No.6 Hamidi Begum and also identified the deponent. It is therefore clear that D.W.1 S.M. Anwar is on the contrary in collusion with his brother defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique in order to cheat the plaintiff and make illegal gain. 

 transfer 8 gandas 1 kara of the suit plot in favour of the plaintiff on 4-9-74. It is clear that on 4-9-74 while executing Ext.6 defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique on behalf of Wakf Estate defendant No.1 received Taka 1,15,000/- from the plaintiff. The defendant No.2 S.M. Siddique has not denied his signature in Ext.6 by deposing in the Court. On the other hand he admitted in his written statement to have put his signature in his letter head slip but in a vain attempt to resile from the contract came with a false story that he put his signature in a blank letter head sheet. P.W.1 Abdul Malek Soudagar and P.W.2 Md. Sayedul Haque have proved the signatures and contents of the document Ext.6. 

 14. We have also shown that from the evidence of P.W.1 Abdul Malek Sowdagar (the plaintiff), P.W.3 Md. Hemayetulla and P.W.4 M.A. Hassan (defendant No.7) it has been proved beyond any doubt that the plaintiff paid. a further sum of Taka 81,730/- as part of the consideration money of the agreement Ext.6 dated 4.9.74 to defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum on behalf of the Wakf Estate to rescind the earlier agreement and to obtain the deed of cancellation. 

 Receipt Ext.9 and the Pass Book Ext.11 it is also proved, as already shown, that the plaintiff paid Taka 30001- to the Wakf Estate defendant No.1 through the Mutawalli defendant No.2 on 18-12-74 as part of consideration money for the suit land. 

 18. Mr. S.C. Das, the learned Advocate for the appellant submits that clause 19 of the deed of lease Ext.5 dated 24-1-67 executed between the C.D.A. Defendant No.5 and the Wakf Estate defendant No.1 provides, "That the tenant shall not sell, charge, mortgage, exchange, gift away or otherwise assign, sublet, encumber or in any way part with or dispose of the demised property or any part thereof before the construction of the buildings, and appurtenances hereby covenanted to be erected and such transfers, etc., if any shall be void." He further submits that under this term the transfer before construction would be void and therefore the contract for transfer is also void. He relies on section 23 of the Contract Act and submits that the contract of transfer is void because the transfer if permitted would defeat the provisions of the agreement for lease which has the force of law and because the transfer is opened to public policy. It is difficult to accept the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the lease agreement has the force of a law. The contention that the leasee is a statutory authority and therefore the terms of the lease have also the force of law is also not acceptable. The contract between the plaintiff and the defendant has to be examined in the light of the provisions of the Contract Act and the terms of the lease agreement. The contract is not hit by section 23 of the Contract Act as it in not in contravention of any law. The learned Advocate for the appellant refers to section 29 of the Contract Act and submits that the agreement is void for uncertainty because its meaning is not certain and is not capable of being made certain. We have gone through the memo of agreement Ext 6. The learned Advocate attacked it on the ground that it does not provide the exact situation of the 8 gandas 1 kara of land in the C.D.A. plot No.5. There is no evidence that there is any subsequent agreement between the parties specifying positively the land to be transferred. This however does not make the agreement uncertain. There can be a valid agreement with respect to an undivided quantity of land of a specific plot. In such agreement the subject matter is a specific share described in quantum out of a specific plot of which number and identity have been specifically given. There is no uncertainty about the suit plot. The instant agreement is therefore not hit by section 29 of the Contract Act also. It may be stated that admittedly the earlier agreement between Wakf Estate defendant No.1 and defendant No.6 Mrs. Hamidi Begum was in respect of specified northern portion (measuring 8 gandas 1 kara) of the C.D.A. plot No.5, Jubilee Road, Chittagong. The documents Ext. 1 and Ext.2 have been referred to in item No.7 of the memo of Ext. 6. Therefore it is clear that the parties intended to transfer the specified northern. 8 gandas 1 kara of the suit plot No.5. 

 19. As regards the contention of the learned Advocate that the contract of transfer if enforced would bring about a transfer which is hit by clause 19 of the C.D.A.'s lease agreement Ext.5 dated .24-1-67 under which transfer before the construction of the building has been prohibited and made void, it may be stated that this contention would have prevailed if subsequently the C.D.A. defendant No.5 would not have by resolution dated 12-11-74 Ext.18 provided that if allottes makes full payment of all the dues and if the allotment was made at least 5 years before the date of application of transfer of unconstructed plot or portion of a plot may be allowed provided transfer fee of Taka 500/-only per katta or part is paid to C.D.A. This resolution of the C.D.A. clearly waives the restriction on the transfer of unconstructed plot or part thereof as provided in clause 19 of the lease agreement Ext.5. The allotment in favour of defendant No.1 was made by the C.D.A. defendant No.5 much more than 5 years before the present agreement. The learned Advocates for both the appellant and respondent submitted that the entire consideration money for the suit plot have been paid by defendant No.1 to defendant No.5 C.D.A. Obtaining of permission for transfer in terms of resolution dated 12-11-74 Ext.18 on payment of the necessary transfer fee is now a matter of formality which does not stand in the way of enforcement of specific performance of contract against the defendant No.1 Therefore in view of the waiver of clause 19 of the lease agreement Ext.5 by the resolution of the C.D.A. dated 12-11-74 Ext.18 referred to above the said clause 19 now does not stand in the way of transfer of unconstructed plot or portion thereof and consequently specific performance of the present contract is enforceable. In this connection the decision in the case of Mansoor Husmain others V. Wali Mohammad & others, 17 D.L.R. (S.C.) 369 P.L.D. 1965 (S.C.) 425 may be referred to. In that case it was argued that if the contract were enforced, it would violate certain provisions of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act. The Pakistan Supreme Court held that reading the provisions embodided in the relevant section of the said Act it would appear that the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act does not forbid the making of contract which may contemplate doing a thing which is contrary to the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, for that a thing can still be done by expost facto permission of the State Bank of Pakistan. In the instant case the lease agreement between the C.D.A. and defendant No.1 does not forbid the making of a contract which may contemplate transfer of unconstructed plot or part thereof which is contrary to the original lease agreement between the C.D.A. and the Wakf Estate, as such provision may be waived and has in fact been waived by the resolution Ext.18 dated 12-11-74. On the principle enunciated in this decision reported in 17 D.L.R. (S.C.) 369 also the contract between the plaintiff and defendant No.1 cannot be said to be hit by clause 19 of the agreement. In the decision reported in 17 D.L.R. (S.C.) 369 the relationship between the parties was governed by the provision of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act and in the case before us the relationship between the parties is governed by the terms of the lease agreement. The principle involved however is the same. 

 20. The learned Advocate for the appellant Submits that no specific sanction of the Administrator of Wakf to transfer the suit land to the plaintiff has been obtained and in the absence of any permission the contract cannot be enforced. It appears from the sanction letter Ext. X dated 30-3-66 of the Administrator of Wakf defendant No.4 that previous Mutawalli Md. Yahia was permitted to transfer 9 gandas of land out of 14 gandas allotted to the Wakf Estate by the C.D.A. This sanction is a general sanction to transfer 9 gandas out of 14 gandas allotted to the Wakf Estate without any condition. The 14 gandas is identifiable with C.D.A. plot No.5, Jubilee Road which was admittedly the plot allotted by C.D.A. of the defendant No.1 Wakf Estate. The permission granted by the Administrator of Wakfs is general and does not say that permission to transfer is in favour of a particular person. Just because at the time the permission was obtained there was a contract of sale with defendant No.6 Hamidi Begum (wife of defendant No.7) it cannot be said that after the contract with defendant No.6 Hamidi Begum was rescinded, the sanction will not continue to remain valid for a transfer to any other person, in the instant case to the plaintiff. It is not the case of the defendant that the permission has been rescinded by the Administrator of Wakfs and the permission must, therefore, be held to hold good still. The learned Advocate could not show us any provision of law requiring that permission for transfer should be in favour of a particular person. It is evident that permission to transfer land by the Wakf Estate granted by the Wakf Administrator as reflected in the sanction letter Ext. X is sufficient. 

 21. The learned Advocate for the appellant submits that if the defendant is permitted to transfer 8 gandas out of 14 gandas, practically nothing of the plot allotted to the Wakf Estate will remain and if the contract is enforced it will cause extreme hardship to the beneficiaries of the Wakf Estate including the present Mutawalli. The learned Advocate has placed reliance on the decision in the case of Administrator of Wakfs and another V, Most. Sahera Begum Chwodhurani and others, 28 D.L.R. 238. In that case two residential houses in the city of Dhaka constituting the only tangible assets of the Wakf were to be transferred, the only other property being a cloth shop at Patuatully the business of which had come to complete stop by the time the suit for enforcement of the contract was being heard. A Division Bench of this Court held that it was a case of extreme hardship which was likely to result from the performance of the contract and further that having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case it was a fit case in which the discretionary power of the Court to refuse specific performance of contract should be exercised. Ext. G is the deed of Wakf dated 12-2-1919. In the case before us no case has been made out that the property contracted to be transferred was even a substantial part of the assests of the Wakf and that if the contract is enforced, it would be a case of extreme hardship. In the instant case the Wakf Estate, which has many other properties, contracted to transfer the suit property for the purpose of acquiring a more valuable property for the benefit of the Wakf Estate. The principle of law enunciated in the reported decision in 28 D.L.R. 238 is not attracted and we are unable to consider it to be a fit case in which we should exercise our discretion by refusing specific performance of the contract. It would evidently be unjust to the plaintiff if he is otherwise entitled to get a decree for specific performance. It may also be noted that in the case reported in 28 D.L.R. 238 the Administrator of Wakfs had revoked the earlier permission to transfer and the appeal was filed by the Administrator of the Wakf.
